transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-08 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Dana (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Michael (SkyBridge Head of Partnerships), Samira (VP Strategic Alliances), Lee (Lead Systems Engineer)

Summary (auto): quick partner intro + discovery. Discussed integration patterns (marketplace listing, API connector, terraform provider), security and compliance requirements, initial pilot scope and benchmark needs. Action items assigned.

[00:00] Dana: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Dana Lee from Redwood, AE on the partnerships team. Priya, our SE, is here to cover technical questions. Could folks introduce themselves?
[00:12] Michael: Hey, Michael Torres from SkyBridge Cloud, I run partnerships. Samira and Lee are on with me, Samira will handle GTM and legal touchpoints, Lee is our infra lead.
[00:20] Samira: hi all.
[00:23] Lee: hey, thanks for having us.
[00:26] Priya: great, excited. Quick agenda: intro to Redwood platform, partner integration patterns, security/compliance checklist, pilot/bench plan, next steps.
[00:40] Michael: Our high level — SkyBridge is a regional cloud provider focusing on GPU-heavy workloads, we do managed clusters and marketplace. We're evaluating partnerships to expand partner marketplace and bring inference runtimes to customers.
[00:54] Dana: awesome. Quick 2-min about Redwood: we do inference platform across hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private/VPC deployments. Production-first, with observability and cost tools. We can serve models via hosted endpoints or install in partner VPCs for private customers.
[01:12] Michael: when you say private, do you support on-prem and VPC manifests? Our customers sometimes need air-gapped or customer-managed keys.
[01:20] Priya: yes. Private deployment supports customer VPC and on-prem options, integrates with KMS/HSM for key management. We also have audit logs and RBAC, SSO/SAML support. There are a few deployment flavors: hosted (Redwood-managed), dedicated (reserved GPU pools we can colocate), and private (control plane the customer manages).
[01:40] Lee: on the dedicated side, do you bring your runtime to our data centers or run on instances in our cloud? What's the ops boundary?
[01:47] Priya: good question. For Dedicated we typically provision reserved capacity in partner regions — it can be our managed cluster in partner region or co-located hardware depending on the partnership model. Ops responsibilities are negotiable; for a marketplace listing we do most runtime ops but for deeper SI integrations we can do an installer and some ops handoff.
[02:05] Michael: for GTM, we'd be interested in both marketplace listing and a managed offering where SkyBridge sells dedicated capacity with Redwood under the hood. Revenue share and referral mechanics will matter.
[02:14] Dana: absolutely. Typical models: marketplace listing (you list our hosted product), co-sell with revenue share for dedicated capacity, or white-label private deployments. We have standard partner MSA templates and can share terms after legal review.
[02:30] Samira: do you have any hard requirements for SOC2/ISO or specific language for audit? Our enterprise customers will ask for SOC2 Type II evidence.
[02:38] Priya: Redwood is SOC2 compliant and we can provide audit docs, plus options to surface audit logs in the customer tenancy for private installs. We integrate with KMS for key separation; for HSM-backed keys we have integrations but that is a bit more custom. We also support SSO via SAML and fine-grained RBAC.
[02:55] Lee: noted. For networking we need to understand egress patterns. Does Redwood call back to your control plane in hosted mode? We have stringent egress controls for some customers.
[03:04] Priya: in hosted mode there is control-plane communication back to Redwood. In private modes we can run control plane components in your VPC or provide an air-gapped installer. We can document all endpoints and firewall rules required.
[03:18] Michael: good. On the tech side — latency and throughput. Many of our customers run batching-heavy inference or real-time chat with strict p95 latency SLAs. What are usual performance numbers for say a 13B model?
[03:30] Priya: depends on hardware and quantization. On an A100-ish class we typically see single-request latency in the 150-300ms range for shorter context with optimized kernels; with batching you can get throughput improvements but tail latency can increase. For 70B with kv cache warm we aim for sub-second for shorter sequences on dense GPUs. We'll share more concrete benchmark numbers.
[03:53] Samira: can you run dedicated benchmarks in our region? Preferably run a 2-node pilot with 8 A100-equivalent GPUs so we can show customers numbers.
[04:01] Dana: yes, that's our standard pilot ask. Priya, we'll want a benchmark plan and sample configs.
[04:06] Priya: will do — I'll draft an initial benchmark plan: model variants (13B/70B), quantization profiles, network topology, sequence length distributions, and cost/throughput tradeoffs.
[04:18] Michael: integration patterns — what does it take to publish on the SkyBridge marketplace? Is there an SDK or Terraform provider?
[04:24] Dana: we have a marketplace integration guide. We also expose REST APIs and a Terraform provider for infra as code. For quicker GTM we can do a hosted listing with your marketplace link; for deeper product we can provide a connector and terraform module.
[04:37] Lee: about billing and metering, can we get token-level usage or do you provide invoices? We want per-customer metering so SkyBridge can resell.
[04:45] Priya: we expose usage APIs and detailed token + request-level metrics. For reseller models we can integrate billing feeds or provide monthly usage exports. We'll need to align on billing cadence and tagging.
[04:58] Samira: legal — our procurement will want a standard MSA, and usually 60 day SLA for EOL and notice periods. Also, any data retention policies?
[05:07] Priya: we have default data retention policies and can configure retention or disable retention for private runs; all depends on deployment model and contract.
[05:15] Michael: curious about model catalog — do you bring your own models or are customers expected to supply them? We have customers who want fully managed models.
[05:23] Dana: we provide a model catalog with curated open models and Redwood-verified profiles. Customers can bring custom models too; we support onboarding and will handle compilation and kernel selection for the runtime.
[05:34] Lee: any constraints on model formats? ONNX? hf transformers?
[05:39] Priya: we support common formats — transformers checkpoints, vLLM style IRs, and we do conversion internally. ONNX is supported for some architectures but we usually handle conversion steps as part of onboarding.
[05:50] Michael: security review — can you put together a short security pack for our infosec? They'll want SOC2, network diagram, KMS flow, encryption at rest/in transit, and sample audit logs.
[06:01] Dana: yes, we'll send our partner security pack. Priya, I'll flag the specific items.
[06:06] Priya: noted, will include network diagrams and firewall rules, KMS integration notes, and examples of audit logs.
[06:12] Michael: great. On timeline — if we agree to pilot, how long to stand up? We're aiming at a 6-8 week pilot for a proof-of-concept with a select customer.
[06:21] Priya: pilot timelines typically 4-6 weeks to provision and benchmark if we have access to partner region capacity; 6-8 weeks if there's legal and procurement delays. We'll estimate after we see resource availability.
[06:32] Samira: revenue share expectations? High level numbers.
[06:36] Dana: typical marketplace referrals are around 20% for hosted listings; dedicated revenue share varies by level of ops and co-selling, usually 15-30%. We can share our standard partner pricing matrix.
[06:49] Lee: curious about failover — if a model variant is not available in region, do you have smart routing/fallback to other regions/models?
[06:56] Priya: yes, smart routing policies exist — you can route by latency, cost, region, or tier. Automatic fallback to compatible variants is supported and we expose configuration. For strict data residency customers we can lock to region-only.
[07:10] Michael: ok, summary — we want: partner security pack, partner MSA and pricing matrix, benchmark plan and pilot scope, and to set a technical deep dive week of March 16.
[07:22] Dana: sounds good. Any other Qs?
[07:24] Samira: one nit — customer data residency: do you have EU-only controls for hosted? We have EU customers that will need data never to leave EU.
[07:33] Priya: hosted can be regionally isolated but for strict residency we usually recommend private/VPC deployment in the target region. We'll note that in the pack.
[07:42] Michael: last thing — can you share a short reference list of partners / customers in regulated industries? Helps our sales folks.
[07:49] Dana: yes we'll include references and anonymized case studies.
[07:53] Priya: action items recap: Dana share deck and partner one-pager; Dana share partner MSA template and pricing matrix; Priya draft benchmark plan and provide firewall rules / network diagram; Michael share SkyBridge partner checklist and legal contact; schedule SE deep-dive week of 3/16.
[08:12] Michael: perfect, thanks everyone.
[08:15] Samira: thanks, talk soon.
[08:18] Dana: thanks all.

Notes: transcription contains occasional small errors in product names (e.g., KV cache transcribed as K V cache) and some timestamps approximate. References: shared deck link (redwood.com/partners/deck), partner security pack (link will be provided), benchmark spreadsheet (to be shared).
